patch_description: The current program runs a fixed 30 greedy restarts and then one local search descent, so it can only escape local optima via Or-opt moves of length ≤3. I propose two changes: (1) wrap the whole pipeline in a time budget (~25s) so restarts and refinement adapt to actual runtime rather than a fixed count; (2) add a ruin-and-recreate perturbation loop — remove 3–8 random transactions, greedily reinsert each at its best position, and run the local search on the perturbed solution, accepting it only if it improves the best. This is a well-known Large Neighborhood Search pattern: ruining breaks the structural bias of the greedy construction while greedy reinsertion keeps solutions high-quality, letting the descent escape local minima that swap/Or-opt cannot. Empirically this gains significant makespan over plain local moves at identical construction settings.
